criteria.evidence: Every section the guidance asks for is present and substantive: What it does ("Runs after the setup answers are confirmed. It records which rule groups of the review fit the project..."), Inputs / Outputs ("Out: the project's rule-group record, kept in the product profile... one entry per rule group: the group's name, kept or skipped, and the question and answer that decided it"), Rules & behavior (six answer-to-group mappings plus the default-keep rule), five Given/When/Then criteria, Out of scope naming each owner, and an Agent intent (ICE) section with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by lines.

Items carry their why: "A database group on a project with no database gives only noise, but a group skipped by mistake hides real findings, so only a clear answer can skip one."; "Database no: the database group is skipped, because there is no schema, query or data store for its rules to check."; "it is never skipped by another answer, because a leak of personal data is the costliest miss."; "kept in the product profile beside the setup answers, so the review reads it where every later play reads the project's facts."

Discrete bullets throughout, the feature states the function's behavior ("It records which rule groups of the review fit the project and which do not"), never a user story, and acceptance is Given/When/Then: "Given answers that say there is no front end, no back-end service, no database and no running service, when the rule groups are chosen, then the record marks those four groups as skipped, each with the answer that decided it."

The parent gives one line: "Choose the review rule groups (fn-review-rule-groups): records which rule groups of the review fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped." The feature adds the record's shape ("one entry per rule group: the group's name, kept or skipped, and the question and answer that decided it"), the answer-to-group mapping for six groups, the default-keep edge case, the personal-data override and the Garura-specific permission case, so detail clearly increases.

The node's core term is never defined: "It records which rule groups of the review fit the project" (a cold reader must infer that a rule group is a set of review rules that check one concern, such as database or front end). Two lines also point at a file the reader cannot see: "see the manifest's gaps" and "Our default, held in the manifest's gaps."
criteria.fix: Add a first bullet to What it does that defines the term, for example: "A rule group is a set of the review's rules that check one kind of thing (front end, back-end service, database, running service, permissions, personal data); the review runs or skips a group as a whole." Replace both "the manifest's gaps" references with the gap stated in the doc itself, for example: "(open question: the sources do not list every rule group the review has)" and "(open question: Garura's answer to the permissions question is not yet recorded)".
